text: Assumption 1 . The set $\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is convex and bounded with diameter $D\doteq\sup_{\bm{x},\bm{y}\in\mathcal{X}}\|\bm{x}-\bm{y}\|$ and radius $R\doteq\sup_{\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}}\|\bm{x}\|$ .

Assumption 2 . The loss $f_{t}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}$ is twice differentiable, convex, $G$ -Lipschitz, and $\beta$ -smooth; i.e., $\|\nabla f_{t}(\bm{x})\|\leq G,\qquad\nabla^{2}f_{t}(\bm{x})\preceq\beta I,\qquad\forall t\in[T],\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}.$
Assumption 3 . The switching coefficients $\{\lambda_{t}\}_{t=2}^{T}$ satisfy $0<\lambda_{t}\leq\lambda$ for a known constant $\lambda>0$ .
Assumption 4 . There exists $M_{f}>0$ such that $0\leq f_{t}(\bm{x})\leq M_{f},\quad\forall t\in[T],\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ .

Theorem 5 (Dynamic regret of FPRLL) . If $\mathrm{FPRLL}$ is run with $\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}$ , then for any $\sigma,\mu>0$ , $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}}\right]\leq\frac{G^{2}}{2\sigma}T+R\sqrt{2d}\,\mu+(TG+\sigma R)P_{T}+\bigl(CG_{c}P_{T}+GR\bigr)\sqrt{T}+\lambda T\Big(\frac{\beta d}{\sigma}{+}\frac{\sqrt{d}\,G}{\mu}\Big)+\frac{\sigma}{2}R^{2}+1.$ In particular, choosing $\mu^{\star}=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda GT}{R\sqrt{2}}},\qquad\sigma^{\star}=\sqrt{\frac{(G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d)\,T}{R^{2}}},$ yields $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}}\right]\leq(R+P_{T})\sqrt{(G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d)\,T}+3\sqrt{\lambda dRGT}+TG\,P_{T}+\bigl(CG_{c}P_{T}+GR\bigr)\sqrt{T}+1.$

Corollary 6 (Static regret on a block) . Consider $\mathrm{FPRLL}$ , and let $I=\{(j-1)k+1,\dots,jk\}$ be any full restart block. On this block, the algorithm is restarted and run with $\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}},\mu^{\star}_{k}=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda Gk}{R\sqrt{2}}},\sigma^{\star}_{k}=\frac{\sqrt{(G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d)\,k}}{R}.$ Then, for every fixed comparator $\bm{u}\in\mathcal{X}$ , $\displaystyle\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{I}(\bm{u})}\right]$ $\displaystyle\doteq\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t\in I}\bigl(f_{t}(\bm{x}_{t})-f_{t}(\bm{u})\bigr)+\lambda\sum_{t=(j-1)k+1}^{jk}\mathbf{1}\{x_{t}\neq x_{t-1}\}\Big]$ $\displaystyle\leq R\sqrt{(G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d)\,k}+3\sqrt{\lambda dRG\,k}+GR\sqrt{k}+\lambda+1=C_{\mathrm{base}}\sqrt{k},$ where $C_{\mathrm{base}}\doteq R\sqrt{G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d}+3\sqrt{\lambda dRG}+GR+\lambda+1.$

Theorem 7 (A dyadic restart scale) . Assume for simplicity that $T$ is a power of two, and let $\mathcal{H}\doteq\{1,2,4,\dots,T\}$ . For each $k\in\mathcal{H}$ , FPRLL $(k)$ uses within each block the tuning $\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}},\ \mu^{\star}_{k}=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda Gk}{R\sqrt{2}}},\ \sigma^{\star}_{k}=\frac{\sqrt{(G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d)\,k}}{R}.$ Define the constants $A\doteq C_{\mathrm{base}}+\lambda,\ B\doteq\sqrt{G^{2}+2\lambda\beta d}+CG_{c}.$ Then there exists a dyadic restart scale $k^{\dagger}\in\mathcal{H}$ such that $\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1},{{k^{\dagger}}}}_{T}\;\leq\;\sqrt{2}\,\min_{1\leq k\leq T}\left(A\frac{T}{\sqrt{k}}+(B+G)P_{T}\,k\right).$ In particular, for $P_{T}=\mathcal{O}(T^{\alpha})$ , $\alpha\in[0,1)$ , $\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1},{{k^{\dagger}}}}=\mathcal{O}\big(T^{2/3}P_{T}^{1/3}\big).$

Theorem 8 (Tracking lower bound) . Consider online linear optimization on $\mathcal{X}=[-1,1]$ with losses $f_{t}(x)=g_{t}x$ , $g_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}$ . Let $\tau\geq 1$ and $T\geq 4\tau$ . There exists a distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over oblivious loss sequences such that, for every integer $k\in[4,\,T/\tau]$ , FPRLL $(k)$ run against $\mathcal{D}$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(u_{1:T})\bigr]\;=\;\Omega\left(\frac{k\tau}{\log(T/\tau)}\right)$ for the associated comparator sequence with $S_{T}(u_{1:T})=\tau$ and $P_{T}(u_{1:T})=2\tau$ .

Theorem 12 (Strongly adaptive regret) . For every interval $I=[s,e]\subseteq[T]$ of length $L=e-s+1$ , $\mathrm{SAR}_{I}(\bm{u})\leq C_{\mathrm{base}}C_{\mathrm{gc}}\sqrt{L}+C_{\mathrm{dm}}\,C_{\mathrm{gc}}\sqrt{M(M+\lambda)L\log(KT)}+\lambda\bigl(2\lceil\log_{2}L\rceil+1\bigr)=\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{L}).$ (13)

Corollary 13 (Dynamic regret, $S_{T}$ branch) . For every comparator sequence, Algorithm 2 attains $\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(\{\bm{u}_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T})\bigr]\;\leq\;\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{(S_{T}+1)\,T}\right)+\lambda\,S_{T}.$

Theorem 14 (Dynamic regret, $P_{T}$ branch) . For every comparator sequence, Algorithm 2 attains $\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(\{\bm{u}_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T})\bigr]\;\leq\;\min_{H\in\mathcal{H}}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}g_{t}^{(H)}-\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(\bm{u}_{t})\right)\;+\;C_{\mathrm{dm}}\sqrt{M(M+\lambda)\,T\log(KT)}.$ (14) In particular, for $H=k^{\dagger}$ from Theorem 7 , we obtain $\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(\{\bm{u}_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T})\bigr]\;=\;\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\max\left\{T^{2/3}P_{T}^{1/3},\,\sqrt{T}\right\}\right).$ (15)

Theorem 17 . Consider the one-dimensional problem on $\mathcal{X}=[-1,1]$ with linear losses $f_{t}(x)=g_{t}x,\qquad g_{t}\in\{-1,+1\}.$ Let the learner predict at each round $\displaystyle x_{t}\doteq\argmin_{x\in(-1,1)}\Big\{F_{t}(x)+\langle{G_{0}+p_{t}},{x}\rangle\Big\}=\argmin_{x\in(-1,1)}\Big\{\langle{G_{t-1}+p_{t}},{x}\rangle+r_{t}(x)+b(x)\Big\},$ (19) where $G_{t-1}=G_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}g_{i}$ , for an arbitrary $G_{0}\in\mathbb{R}$ , $b(x)=-\frac{1}{M_{\gamma}}\log(1-x^{2})$ is the logarithmic barrier for $\mathcal{X}$ , $r_{t}(x)=\frac{\sigma_{t}}{2}x^{2}$ with $\sigma_{t}\geq 0$ , and $p_{t}$ are arbitrary symmetric perturbations. Then, there exists an oblivious loss sequence and a one-switch comparator sequence such that $\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t})-f_{t}(u_{t})\bigr)\right]\;\geq\;\frac{T}{2}.$

Corollary 18 . Under the assumptions of Theorem 17 , let $T=2n$ and consider the oblivious loss sequence $g_{t}=\begin{cases}-1,&t\leq n,\\ +1,&t>n,\end{cases}\qquad u_{t}=-g_{t}.$ Then $\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t})-f_{t}(u_{t})\bigr)\right]\;\geq\;\frac{T}{2}.$

Proposition 20 (Combined lower bound) . Consider the following two full-horizon adversaries: 1. the adversary from Theorem 8 , together with comparator sequence $u^{\mathrm{gad}}_{1:T}$ , for which $S_{T}(u^{\mathrm{gad}}_{1:T})=\tau,\qquad P_{T}(u^{\mathrm{gad}}_{1:T})=2\tau,$ and $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(u^{\mathrm{gad}}_{1:T})}\right]=\Omega\left(\frac{k\tau}{\log(T/\tau)}\right);$ 2. the adversary from Lemma 19 , together with the stationary comparator sequence $u^{\mathrm{sh}}_{1:T}\equiv u^{\star}$ , for which $S_{T}(u^{\mathrm{sh}}_{1:T})=0,\qquad P_{T}(u^{\mathrm{sh}}_{1:T})=0,$ and $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(u^{\mathrm{sh}}_{1:T})}\right]=\Omega\left(\frac{T}{\sqrt{k}}\right).$ For the fixed restart period $k$ , define a mixed adversary that, at time $0$ , chooses one of these two branches uniformly at random and then plays the chosen branch for the entire horizon. The resulting mixed adversary may depend on $k$ through the Sherman branch. Let $u_{1:T}$ denote the comparator sequence associated with the realized branch. Then $\mathop{\mathbb{E}}\left[{\mathcal{R}^{\mathbf{1}}_{T}(u_{1:T})}\right]=\Omega\left(\frac{k\tau}{\log(T/\tau)}+\frac{T}{\sqrt{k}}\right).$
